title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
A generative AI system was used to create pornographic deepfake videos depicting real women without their consent. The videos were hosted on a platform that reached millions of visitors monthly and featured Dutch public figures including politicians, athletes, and entertainers. This is a case of impersonation through synthetic media, where a model generated false sexual imagery bearing the likenesses of identifiable people.

The deployment of deepfake generation technology had no apparent safeguards against misuse for creating non-consensual sexual content. A human review system or content moderation policy could have prevented the videos from being hosted and distributed at scale. The harm occurred because the technology was available for abuse and the platform did not block such material.

It is not established whether the same person created all the videos, whether the platform knowingly hosted them, or what technical measures would have been feasible to detect and remove them automatically. A previous case resulted in a conviction, but this incident shows the problem persisted.

summary:
Multiple well-known Dutch women are considering legal action after their faces were digitally manipulated and placed into pornographic videos. These fake videos appear on an online platform that receives approximately 13 million monthly visitors. The platform hosts numerous deepfake pornography videos featuring Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Interim Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file complaints with authorities.

Several victims have already filed reports or are exploring legal options, according to their managers and representatives. Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is therefore illegal. Lawyers recommend victims file complaints, which could allow prosecutors to shut down the website. Other available options include starting a class action lawsuit, filing complaints with data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, television presenter Welmoed Sijtsma became a victim of such videos, and a 39-year-old man from Amersfoort was convicted and received a conditional 180-hour work sentence in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
